notes: Historical and forecast drivers are modeled using EBIT margin as Operating Income / Revenue from KMI’s consolidated statements; DD&A corresponds to “depreciation, depletion and amortization” from the income statement.

NWC level is computed as Total current assets minus Total current liabilities using GAAP balance sheet totals; this includes items beyond the typical unlevered working-capital definition (e.g., cash and debt-related current items). This definition likely drives negative NWC levels and is flagged for DCF QA/interpretation. ([s24.q4cdn.com](https://s24.q4cdn.com/126708163/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/KMI-2024-10K-Final-wo-Exhibits.pdf))

Capital expenditures are GAAP “Capital expenditures” from the cash flow statement for 2023-2024, and GAAP capex from the 4Q25 financial results release for 2025. ([s24.q4cdn.com](https://s24.q4cdn.com/126708163/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/KMI-2024-10K-Final-wo-Exhibits.pdf))

WACC is approximated using: risk-free proxy from FRED DGS10 near the as-of period, KMI beta from Yahoo Finance, an implied US equity risk premium from Damodaran’s January 2026 dataset, and an after-tax cost of debt approximated using cash paid for interest (2024 10-K) and the tax-rate estimate. Exact practitioner WACC inputs may differ. ([fred.stlouisfed.org](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10))

Comps NTM multiples (EV/NTM Revenue, EV/NTM EBITDA, P/NTM) are set to null because they were not captured from a primary/consensus dataset in this pass; populate from Bloomberg/Capital IQ for production use.

NOL utilization percent is set to null because a specific utilization rate (as a percent) is not explicitly disclosed; only carryforward balances (deferred tax assets / NOL amounts) are provided in the referenced 10-K tax footnote. ([s24.q4cdn.com](https://s24.q4cdn.com/126708163/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/KMI-2024-10K-Final-wo-Exhibits.pdf))

net_debt_override uses KMI’s reported Net Debt figure for consistency with company leverage reporting, which may not reconcile exactly to debt minus cash depending on definition components (e.g., fair value adjustments/FX impacts). ([ir.kindermorgan.com](https://ir.kindermorgan.com/news/news-details/2026/Kinder-Morgan-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx))
All currency amounts are presented in full USD units (not millions). Negative NWC reflects the GAAP current-asset/current-liability arithmetic noted above.

catalysts: Regulatory and permitting progress for system expansion projects (e.g., FERC timing and approvals) that can shift utilization and long-run growth expectations.
Quarterly updates on capex execution, placed-in-service timing, and throughput associated with expansion projects and open seasons.
company_overview: Kinder Morgan is a U.S. midstream infrastructure operator with major natural gas pipeline, products pipeline, terminals, and CO2-related businesses (USD reporting currency).
Operating performance is driven by contracted/fee-based transportation and handling volumes, expansion project execution, and disciplined capital allocation.
Capital investment is used to expand throughput and support long-term utilization, while leverage management targets Net Debt-to-EBITDA within a defined range.
current_context: Preliminary 2025 results: revenue $16.937 billion and operating income (EBIT) $4.724 billion; depreciation, depletion & amortization (DD&A) $2.453 billion.
2025 capital expenditures (GAAP) were $3.026 billion; balance sheet shows Net Debt of about $31.716 billion at year-end.
Quarterly dividend declared at $0.2925 per share for Q4 2025 (payable February 17, 2026 to holders of record February 2, 2026).
investment_highlights: Base-case uses a stable-to-slightly-improving EBIT margin profile (~0.283 to 0.285) consistent with recent operating income and revenue relationships.
Revenue growth is modeled as moderate and cyclical-neutral (3.5% in 2026 tapering to 2.5% by 2030) rather than assuming step-changes.
Capital intensity (capex as a percent of sales) starts elevated in the forecast and gradually tapers, reflecting maintaining and sustaining assets while still funding expansion.
Working capital is assumed to remain structurally negative but to improve gradually toward a less-negative level (negative nwc_pct_sales).
key_risks: Regulatory and construction execution risk (cost overruns, schedule delays, or denial/deferral of approvals).
Leverage/credit risk if cash flows underperform and Net Debt-to-EBITDA rises above internal targets.
Commodity and volume-linked risk (even for fee-based models, utilization and revenue mix can be impacted by demand trends).

valuation_summary: DCF framework employs a gordon-growth terminal approach with a 2.0% long-run growth rate and an internally consistent tax-rate / WACC set derived from market inputs.
Comps are included as a peer set (midstream infrastructure) even though NTM multiple inputs were not captured in this pass.
